issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting instructions about the SealSaloon.stock field: one part directs that 'These should be initialized ... in the constructor of SealSaloon' (instance constructor) while another part requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is incorrect or misleading. This contradiction will confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field initialized at declaration or in a static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) make stock an instance final field and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor, or (B) make stock static (shared) and instruct students to initialize it at the declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem text and UML so both consistently state the same modifier and initialization approach.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires the calculateTotalPrice method to be static (it is listed among methods/attributes that 'must be static'), but the solution implementation defines calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (non-static). This mismatch between the spec and the provided solution is a structural inconsistency and will confuse students about the required method signature and usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the problem statement to allow calculateTotalPrice to be an instance method (remove the 'must be static' requirement) or change the solution (and template) to declare calculateTotalPrice as static with the same signature (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)). Ensure the UML and example usage in the statement reflect the chosen approach.
